images.caption: Figure 1:We propose an automatic tool-generation framework for multimodal search agents. In the example shown, an agent restricted to afixedtool library is bound to its pre-defined primitives and fails on queries that no original tool can directly resolve. Our framework insteadgrowsthe library: the agent operates over an extended tool library that includes newly generated tools and can invoke them freely when solving real queries. Here, the newly generated\toolhlEvent In Image tool resolves the query through finer-grained information verification and image search.

Figure 2:Overview of theToolSmithpipeline: capability gaps mined from agent trajectories on a training pool are filtered through reuse-or-grow against the tool catalog, passed to an LLM that authors each new tool as Python source, and admitted only after verification gates with a feedback-driven retry on rejection.

Figure 3:Entity-first identification (Reed Hastings, $50M Hastings Initiative). The base agent searches without knowing who is in the image and misattributes the donation to Eric Schmidt; the generated\toolhlImage Entity Canonical Name tool resolves the person first, after which a single text search returns the correct year.

Figure 4:Entity-first identification on a person whose visual context provides only vague cues. The base agent guesses “Mississippi” from incidental visual content and returns the wrong pageant; the generated\toolhlCelebrated Person From Image tool produces the canonical identity (Beatrice Luigi Gomez), which makes the event lookup trivial.

Figure 5:Precise region identification on a US map. Without explicit map-region parsing the base agent confuses Oregon with neighboring Washington and returns the wrong governor; the generated\toolhlState Context Lookup tool pins down the highlighted state first, after which the governor lookup succeeds.

Figure 6:Search-ranking steering. The base agent’s generic image search returns multiple election maps and the agent latches onto a Reddit thread about the wrong year; the generated\toolhlEvent Name From Image tool primes the search for an event-name extraction and reorders the results so Wikipedia (1996) outranks Reddit (1968).
